title: Staggered rollforward caused traffic amplification, KV-cache thrash and quarantine recovery
creator: Sanjay Patel
description: Summary: On 2026-03-01 at ~10:12 UTC a staggered rollforward of runtime-1.19 to serve model usr/small-v2 triggered traffic amplification in two regions, which amplified KV-cache churn and caused a capacity surge and delayed rollback. Impact: increased p95 latency (x3) for affected routes and transient 5xx spike for ~18 minutes. Root cause: a sequencing bug in the rollout controller applied partial route updates before completing affinity key migration; the proxy duplicated a non-idempotent canary affinity header, causing a subset of requests to be simultaneously routed to both old and new variants (logical duplication). This duplication doubled effective request load for some backends and evicted prefetched KV-cache entries, increasing token service and GPU backpressure. The controller's rollback path was blocked by a stale version pin on a small subset of model shards, preventing immediate clean rollback and requiring manual evacuation.
postmortem: Root cause: rollout-controller allowed non-atomic route insertion when migrating affinity keys. The proxy misinterpreted duplicate affinity headers as independent sessions, creating duplicate in-flight work. Secondary cause: version pinning logic did not surface a broken pin that prevented rollback; existing health checks only considered model Liveness, not route-consistency. Detection: alerted by alerting rule rollout.p95_latency_increase and Grafana dashboard spike; on-call noticed high 5xxs and page triggered at 10:20 UTC. Containment: traffic quarantined from the new variant at 10:30 UTC, the controller forced version-unpin on three shards at 10:45 UTC, drained queues and scaled Dedicated pools +20% to absorb backpressure. Recovery: full steady-state restored by 10:50 UTC after cache warmup and canary reconfiguration. Lessons: rollouts must remain transactional for route-affinity migrations; rollbacks require stronger pin telemetry and automatic unpin fallbacks; KV-cache eviction patterns must surface as a rollout health signal.
timeline: 2026-03-01 10:12 UTC — Rollforward started: runtime-1.19 deploy initiated in eu-west and us-central (Marisa Gomez)
2026-03-01 10:18 UTC — First latency alert: p95 generation latency increased on canary routes (Alert: rollout.p95_latency_increase) (SLO Monitoring)
2026-03-01 10:20 UTC — On-call triage: observed duplicated affinity header patterns in proxy traces; initial hypothesis of misrouted traffic (Daniel Cho)
2026-03-01 10:27 UTC — Attempts to abort and rollback via controller failed due to version-pinned shards failing unpin step (controller logs show pin mismatch) (Lena Weber)
2026-03-01 10:30 UTC — Quarantine: controller applied quarantine policy to new variant route segments to stop new traffic; began manual draining of outstanding requests (Priya Nair)
2026-03-01 10:45 UTC — Forced unpin: ops forced version-unpin on 3 shards after consenting to risk; rollback succeeded and traffic routed back to stable variants (Omar Haddad)
2026-03-01 10:50 UTC — Recovery: latency returned to baseline after caches warmed and extra capacity autoscaled down (Eve Chen)
2026-03-01 11:05 UTC — Post-incident standup and immediate mitigation checklist created (Sanjay Patel)
impact: Medium: several customer routes experienced elevated latency and transient errors for ~18 minutes. No data loss. A small number of high-throughput customers saw increased token costs during the event.
actions_taken: Quarantine new variant routes to stop new traffic (applied at 10:30 UTC)
Manual forced version-unpin for 3 shards to allow rollback (10:45 UTC)
Drained in-flight requests and scaled Dedicated capacity +20% for 30 minutes
Post-incident runbook created and shared to #incidents and confluence
action_items: ENG-954322: Make route-affinity updates transactional in rollout-controller (owner: Daniel Cho) — add preflight validation and two-phase-commit semantics
ENG-954323: Add duplicate-affinity-header detection and reject non-idempotent header combos at proxy ingress (owner: Lena Weber)
ENG-954324: Improve version-pin telemetry: expose per-shard pin-state and add automatic unpin fallback with human approval logic (owner: Omar Haddad)
ENG-954325: Add KV-cache eviction and churn metrics to rollout health checks and alert on eviction_rate > threshold (owner: Eve Chen)
ENG-954326: Update runbook: include forced-unpin procedure, safe quarantine steps, and escalation matrix (owner: Priya Nair)
ENG-954327: Add pre-rollout chaos test that simulates duplicate header injection and checks for duplication-safe behavior (owner: Marisa Gomez)
ENG-954328: Post-deployment canary validation: require warm-cache verification before allowing >10% traffic shift (owner: Sanjay Patel)
ENG-954329: Add automated canary rollback guard to avoid blocked rollback when pins are stale — implement a bounded retry + operator approval flow (owner: Platform Reliability)
ENG-954330: Run tabletop in next Ops All-hands to walk through the new quarantine/forced-unpin flow (owner: Priya Nair)
owners_note: Follow-ups require coordination between runtime, proxy, and rollout-controller teams. Prioritize transactional route changes and visibility into pin state. Estimated total engineering effort across items: ~8-12 sprint points across multiple teams.
